instructions: In the image at screenshot, is a chart drawn with dark, heavy gridlines, borders, or frames that stand out as strongly as the data marks themselves?

criteria.true: A chart has dark, heavy gridlines, borders, or frames that stand out as strongly as the bars, lines, or points that carry the data.
criteria.false: Every chart's gridlines, borders, and frames are absent, thin, or pale, so the data marks stand out more than they do, or the image shows no chart.

instructions: In the image at screenshot, does a chart carry decoration that shows no data, such as pictures, icons, patterned or textured fills, or ornamental backgrounds behind or inside the marks?

criteria.true: A chart carries decoration that shows no data, such as pictures, icons, patterned or textured fills, or ornamental backgrounds behind or inside the marks.
criteria.false: Every chart is drawn with plain marks, axes, and labels and carries no decoration that shows no data, or the image shows no chart.

instructions: In the image at screenshot, is a chart drawn with a three-dimensional effect, such as bars or pie slices with depth, sides, or a tilted perspective, when the data has no third dimension?

criteria.true: A chart is drawn with a three-dimensional effect, such as bars or slices with depth, visible sides, or a tilted perspective.
criteria.false: Every chart is drawn flat, with no depth, visible sides, or tilted perspective, or the image shows no chart.

instructions: In the image at screenshot, does a pie or donut chart have so many slices that the slices are hard to tell apart and compare?

criteria.true: A pie or donut chart has so many slices that several are thin slivers and the slices are hard to tell apart and compare.
criteria.false: Every pie or donut chart has few enough slices that each is easy to tell apart and compare, or the image shows no pie or donut chart.

instructions: In the image at screenshot, does a chart or map show values that run from low to high with a rainbow of unrelated hues, such as red, yellow, green, and blue, instead of one colour that grows lighter or darker?

criteria.true: A chart or map shows values that run from low to high with a rainbow of unrelated hues, so the colours do not read as an order from low to high.
criteria.false: Values that run from low to high are shown with one colour, or two, that grow lighter or darker in order, or the image shows no such chart or map.

instructions: In the image at screenshot, does a chart tell two series or categories apart only by red and green, with no other difference such as labels, shape, pattern, or lightness?

criteria.true: A chart tells two series or categories apart only by red and green, with no direct labels, shapes, patterns, or clear difference in lightness to tell them apart.
criteria.false: Every chart tells its series apart by something other than a red and green pair alone, such as other hues, direct labels, shapes, patterns, or lightness, or the image shows no chart.

instructions: In the image at screenshot, are the bars or marks of a single series drawn in many different colours that encode nothing, when one colour would show the same data?

criteria.true: The bars or marks of a single series are drawn in many different colours that encode nothing, and one colour would show the same data.
criteria.false: Each chart uses colour only to tell apart series or categories that the legend or labels name, or draws a single series in one colour, or the image shows no chart.

instructions: In the image at screenshot, does a line chart overlay so many lines that cross each other that the lines form a tangle and no single line can be followed?

criteria.true: A line chart overlays so many crossing lines that they form a tangle and no single line can be followed from end to end.
criteria.false: Each line chart has few enough lines, or splits them into separate small charts, so that every line can be followed, or the image shows no line chart.

instructions: In the image at screenshot, does a bar chart's value axis start above zero, so the bars are cut off at the bottom and the differences between them look larger than they are?

criteria.true: A bar chart's value axis starts above zero, so the bars are cut off and the differences between them look larger than they are.
criteria.false: Every bar chart's value axis starts at zero, so bar lengths are in proportion to the values, or the image shows no bar chart.

instructions: In the image at screenshot, is a large headline number on a dashboard shown alone, with no unit, no time period, and no comparison such as a change, a target, or an earlier value?

criteria.true: A large headline number is shown alone, with no unit, no time period, and no comparison such as a change, a target, or an earlier value, so a reader cannot tell whether it is good or bad.
criteria.false: Every large headline number has a unit or label, a time period, and a comparison such as a change, a target, or an earlier value, or the image shows no headline number.
